dedupe_keys.name: edxl have 2 0 hospital availability exchange messaging standard for bed counts services and status oasis and hl7

description: EDXL-HAVE is an open XML messaging standard that lets hospitals and other health facilities report their status to emergency managers in a common format. Version 2.0, a joint specification of the OASIS Emergency Management Technical Committee and HL7 published in 2019, defines messages for a facility's services, bed counts by type, operational status, capacities, resource needs and emergency department ambulance offload, so that first responders, coordinating bodies and hospitals share one picture of the health system during a disaster. The specification is free to download as HTML or PDF together with its XML schemas, and it replaces HAVE 1.0. It belongs to the EDXL family, alongside the Common Alerting Protocol. Coverage is international: the standard is not tied to one country, although adoption varies. Caveats: a message standard, not a dataset; implementations and live feeds are run by regional systems and are rarely open; the OASIS licence mode is royalty-free on reasonable terms, not an open licence. Simulation uses: a ready-made schema for hospital state in emergency response models and digital twins, and for exchanging simulated bed availability between tools. Related records: the Common Alerting Protocol (data-oasis-common-alerting-protocol-cap) is the sister standard for warnings, and Portugal's hospital bed and occupancy data (data-sns-portugal-hospital-beds-and-occupancy) show the kind of figures HAVE carries.
